suggested_requirements.text: The CAISO shall review and update the Black Start Capability Plan at least every five years.
The CAISO shall annually verify that the number, size, availability, and location of system Black Start generating units are sufficient to meet WECC restoration plan requirements.
The CAISO shall document Cranking Paths between each Black Start generating unit and the units to be started.
The CAISO shall annually enter into RMR and Interim Black Start Contracts with generators that satisfy the planning evaluation process.
Voluntary Black Start unit owners shall demonstrate at least every five years that the unit can perform its intended functions.
Participants shall submit documentation of Black Start test results and analysis to the CAISO, WECC, or NERC upon request.
Participants shall notify the CAISO RT Dispatcher by phone of the success or failure of a Black Start test within 24 hours of conducting the test.
Participants shall file a letter with the CAISO regarding the success or failure of a Black Start test within 14 days of performing the test.
The CAISO shall maintain a Black Start database containing all Black Start generators designated for use during system restoration.
The CAISO shall review and update the Black Start database on at least an annual basis.
The CAISO shall train Real-time Grid Operators at least annually for system restoration.
Black Start units must be able to self-start without any source of off-site electric power.
Black Start units must maintain adequate voltage and frequency while energizing isolated transmission facilities and auxiliary loads.
Black Start units must maintain voltage within emergency voltage limits over a range of loading from no external load to full external load.
Black Start units must be equipped with governors capable of operating in an isochronous mode.
Black Start units must be capable of starting and energizing the applicable transmission path without assistance from the electrical system.
Hydroelectric generating units or combustion gas turbines must start within 30 minutes of the initiation of the Black Start process.
Industrial gas turbines must start within 60 minutes of the initiation of the Black Start process.
Hot, steam-driven turbines must start within 2.5 hours of the initiation of the Black Start process.
The minimum run time duration of a Black Start test is 10 minutes.
Black Start testing must not endanger the safety of any person, damage equipment, harm the environment, or violate any applicable law, regulation, or operating limit.
